references.role: edit target and exact four-object board and canvas reference

prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit for a modular four-direction strategy-game mining workstation source board. Edit the supplied four-column forge-anvil board into exactly four isolated views of the same compact ore-bearing rock while preserving the source image dimensions (1536x1024), the four-object horizontal layout, generous gaps, and approximately the same object scale and placement. Replace every anvil and wood block completely. Create one coherent knee-high, low angular slate rock with exposed blue-gray iron ore and restrained off-white quartz veins. Give each view a clearly readable chipped strike face aimed toward the worker for that direction. The rock must feel heavy, grounded, and compact, suitable as a mining animation contact target in a classic 1990s real-time strategy game. Use a limited hand-painted pixel-art-like palette, hard deliberate clusters, crisp silhouette, minimal antialiasing, and warm upper-left lantern lighting consistent across all four views. Columns from left to right must be: down/front view, up/back view, left side view, right side view. Author all four directions independently; the side views must not be simple mirrored duplicates. Keep the same rock identity, proportions, ore colors, quartz placement logic, and lighting in every direction. Background must be perfectly flat solid chroma magenta #ff00ff, with no shadows, ground plane, dust, debris, tools, characters, text, borders, labels, wood, anvils, or magenta inside the object. Each rock must be fully contained with wide clear margins and no overlap.
